back: The degree to which a product meets customers' expectations and is fit for its purpose.
Checking products or inputs against a standard, by inspection or testing, to find faults.
A system that prevents faults by setting standards and organising every stage of production, involving all workers.
Feed-forward: check inputs before production. Concurrent: check during production. Feedback: check finished goods and learn from faults.
Every employee is responsible for quality at every stage, aiming for zero defects and customer satisfaction.
A small group of workers who meet regularly to find and solve quality and efficiency problems.
Comparing performance with the best firm to find ways to improve and set targets.
Defect rate (%) = faulty items ÷ items checked × 100. Expected faulty items in a batch = defect rate × batch size.

front: Benefits and costs of quality systems
back: Benefits: fewer returns, less waste, loyalty, higher prices. Costs: inspectors, training, meetings and time.
